newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus nationalists mark former independence day.
newsitem.headline: Belarus nationalists mark former independence day.

text.p: Belarussian nationalists defied official discouragement and marched through the capital Minsk on Sunday to mark the post-Soviet Independence Day holiday scrapped by pro-Russian President Alexander Lukashenko.
About 5,000 people marched under nationalist red and white flags, carrying slogans "Down with Lukashenko!" and "Freedom".
Lukashenko, president since 1994, signed a union treaty with Moscow in April and has cracked down on mostly pro-Western nationalist groups, many of whose leaders have fled the country.

He reintroduced a state flag similar to those used by communist authorities when Belarus was a Soviet republic and switched the celebration of Independence Day from July 27, the day Belarus declared sovereignty within the Soviet Union in 1990, to July 3, when the Red Army freed Minsk from the Germans in 1944.

"A dictatorship has been established in Belarus. But we want to demonstrate our commitment to independence and our negative attitude towards Lukashenko," Nikolai Statkevich, a leader of the opposition Social Democratic Party, told Reuters.

Some foreigners, attending a congress in Minsk of the ethnic Belarussian diaspora, joined the demonstrators. But a rally and rock concert on a central square were reduced to symbolic acts of defiance after city officials refused to provide electricity.
Boris Gyunter, leader of the Belarussian Popular Front, the biggest opposition group, said police raided its offices on Saturday.
"We were told they were searching for weapons. They found nothing -- but took away four flagstaffs," he told Reuters.

Lukashenko's rule has been criticised by international bodies as increasingly authoritarian. He won broad new powers in a controversial referendum last November. About 200 people have been jailed for short terms after previous rallies.
The nationalist opposition is too weak to offer any serious resistance to Lukashenko, who has won popular acclaim with promises of prosperity and closer integration with Russia.
The president has clamped down on critical media.

Russia's biggest television channel, ORT, said on Sunday its correspondent and two of his colleagues in Belarus had been detained by Belarussian frontier guards on Saturday and accused of attempting to cross the Lithuanian border illegally.
Dmitry Novozhylov, an ORT administrator in Minsk, said he was told by frontier officials that ORT reporter Pavel Sheremet and his driver had been arrested on Saturday at Minsk airport.
A duty officer at the State Border Protection Committee would not confirm the detentions when contacted by Reuters.
ORT cameraman Dmitry Zavadsky was arrested at his home in Minsk on Saturday, Novozhylov added, saying all three ORT employees were being held near the Lithuanian border.
Liberals in the Russian government criticised Belarus earlier this month for stripping ORT's Sheremet of his press credentials after accusing him of biased reporting.
Earlier this year, Belarus expelled a reporter for Russia's NTV television, accusing him of unbalanced political reporting.
